propositions: Production in-process verifier achieved 100% per-AC agreement on real ACs with zero false-FAILs and zero evidence-insufficient verdicts across 9 runs.
Minimal free-tool harness agent (Arm B) produced 5 false-FAILs on real ACs (all concentrated on epic 0e68, AC7 and AC2) yielding 94.6% agreement versus 100% for production verifier.

Arm B false-PASS count on planted-unmet ACs was zero, matching Arm A; rejections came from strict literal readings of epic AC clauses (capability-stamp commit scope, enrichment-data presence), not tool constraints.
Production verifier median wall time was 131s; Arm B median was 415.5s (~3× slower), breaching the predeclared rule threshold of ≤2× parity.

Predeclared GO decision rule required (i) zero Arm B false-PASS, (ii) Arm B real-AC rejections < Arm A real-AC rejections, (iii) Arm B median wall ≤ 2× Arm A; conditions (ii) and (iii) both failed (5 < 0 is false; 415.5 ≤ 262 is false).  Result: NO-GO — the hypothesis that unreliability lives in in-process scaffolding rather than the task itself was not supported on this corpus.
